unresolvedMajorIssues: Workout logging screen relies on tiny monospace text and unlabeled icon buttons
Muted and metadata text looks faint in both themes and nothing in the captures confirms it is readable
Primary next action is weak or missing on Today, Routines and Prompts
Screen titles and headers are inconsistent across routes
The routine analysis card is dense and clips content on mobile

findings.evidence: Each exercise card has four small icon-only buttons at the top right: a 'lb' unit toggle, a history clock, a pencil and a swap arrows glyph. None has a visible label. Prescription, set summary and 'add note' are tiny monospace text of roughly 10-11px. The set chips ('135x5', '40x10') look like inputs but also look like static pills. The '+' add-set chip is a faint low-contrast button. The timer shows '--:--' next to play and reset glyphs with no label.
findings.userConsequence: Mid-workout, on a phone, the user has to guess what the pencil, swap and 'lb' controls do, and has to hit small targets. Reading the prescription (3x5 135 lb, rest 2:00) takes effort, and a mis-tap on swap or edit could change the exercise.
findings.suggestedChange: Raise prescription and set text to 13-14px or more. Give the tap targets visible or accessible names (at minimum a visible label on first use, or an overflow menu with text). Make the set chip a clear field with a distinct completed state. Make 'add set' obviously interactive.

findings.evidence: The analysis card stacks a grade badge ('B 89'), the label 'ANALYSIS · 4MS · OFFLINE · PARTIAL' in about 8px monospace, a '3-day program' title, an unlabeled '▼' chevron, a goal select, a five-line explanatory paragraph, and a row of metric tiles. The 'PERIODIZATION ·RE...' tile is clipped at the right edge. The day list below uses a green dot and '▸' with no explanation.
findings.userConsequence: The card takes up half of the first viewport and pushes the actual workout days below it. The clipped tile reads as a layout bug. The grade and 'PARTIAL' label are hard to interpret, and the green dot status is ambiguous, so the user may not know which day to start.
findings.suggestedChange: Collapse the analysis by default into a one-line summary (grade and a 'Details' toggle). Put the day list and a clear 'Start Day 1' action first. Fix the clipped tile (wrap or scroll with a visible affordance). Label the status dot and give the ▼ a text name.

findings.evidence: Secondary text looks very faint. In Library, the row counts (4, 18, 296) and chevrons are pale gray on gray. In History, 'last 10/26' and the version counts are pale on a gray panel. On Today, the '→' glyphs at the right of the onboarding steps are barely visible. In the dark theme, 'UPCOMING' and the Library counts look dim against near-black. No contrast ratios were measured here.
findings.userConsequence: Users with ordinary vision in bright light, such as a gym, may miss the dates, counts and row affordances. The faint chevrons weaken the signal that a row is tappable.
findings.suggestedChange: Raise the muted text and glyph tones in both themes and check them with a contrast tool. Avoid placing mid-gray text on gray-filled panels. Keep dates and counts at primary or secondary text strength.

findings.evidence: On Today (empty), nothing in the three steps reads as a button, so the primary action is only the small 'Go to Profile →' link in a banner that repeats step 1. Roughly 60% of the screen is empty. On Routines, the single routine 'Everyday Strength' shows only '3d/wk · 4w · not started' and an overflow '···'. There is no 'Start' or 'Open' action, and the header says '0 active · 1 draft' with an unexplained orange dot. On Prompts, the preset name field and 'Save' come first. The copy-the-prompt action is only 'at the bottom' of a very long page, per the intro text.
findings.userConsequence: A new user may not realize the steps are tappable. A returning user must open the routine to start training and has to read the status words to know what 'draft' and 'not started' mean. Prompts users have to scroll past long coach text to find the one action that matters for the AI workflow.
findings.suggestedChange: Make the steps full buttons with a clear current step (and drop the duplicated banner). Give the routine row a visible status label plus a primary 'Start' or 'Continue'. On Prompts, use a sticky 'Copy prompt' bar and put the preset controls below the main flow.

findings.evidence: Screen headers differ. Import, History, Library, Prompts and Today use a large bold title. Routines uses a small spaced 'ROUTINES' label with counts and a '+ New' button, with different side margins. Workspace has no title and starts with a 'WORKSPACE' data card. Profile leads with the user's name and avatar. Routine map uses a small caps eyebrow and then a large title. The filter row on Routines starts with an unexplained 'OTHER' label.
findings.userConsequence: The app feels like several different layouts. The 'OTHER' label looks like an error. On Workspace, users get no title confirming they are in settings, which is only reachable through the drawer.
findings.suggestedChange: Define one page header pattern (title, optional one-line meta, one primary action) and apply it to every route. Remove or explain 'OTHER'. Add a visible 'Workspace' title.

findings.evidence: The Import screen shows the browser's raw 'Choose File No file chosen' control with no styling, above a textarea whose content is cut off. The 'Validate →' button is a full-width blue bar with tiny text. In the error state the message 'The provided content is not valid JSON.' is red text with no icon, and the recovery action sits below it as an outlined button with a small helper line. On the Resolve step, the metadata ('imported · strength', 'used 4 times') is set in a small monospace font. In the History export panel, the preview is a clipped monospace block with horizontal truncation. It sits next to empty native 'mm/dd/yyyy' date inputs and two small buttons, 'Copy' and 'Download .txt'.
findings.userConsequence: The offline copy/paste AI workflow is the product's core, but its controls look unfinished. A user may not realize the export text is cut off, or that the empty date fields mean 'all dates'. In the import error the primary 'Validate' stays visually dominant over the recovery action.
findings.suggestedChange: Style the file input as a secondary button next to the paste area. Add a labeled 'Paste' area with a visible character or line count. Show the error in a bordered alert and make 'Copy recovery prompt' the primary action in that state. Make 'Copy' the primary button in the export panel and wrap or scroll the preview with a visible affordance.

findings.evidence: The Library filter chips are cut off at the right edge ('machine' touches the edge, with no sign of scrolling). The 3175-exercise catalog is a flat accordion list of muscle groups, with 'NEEDS REVIEW' first. Profile shows a bodyweight line with no axis or dates, and the heatmap labels (M, W, F, S) and 'streak: 0 · avg: 0.3/wk' are about 9px. The Routine map cards wrap '3 sections · 3 ex' to two lines.
findings.userConsequence: Users may not find the hidden chips, and finding an exercise means opening many groups. The bodyweight chart doesn't communicate a trend or dates, and the heatmap legend needs a good eye.
findings.suggestedChange: Make the chip row obviously scrollable (fade edge) or wrap it. Put the most-used groups first. Add dates to the chart ends and enlarge the heatmap labels. Shorten the map card meta so it fits on one line.

findings.evidence: In mobile-dark/workspace.png the page uses the dark terminal styling but the 'linen' theme chip is the selected one, which contradicts the manifest's 'terminal' theme. This may be a capture-state artifact; the screenshot alone can't tell. On Workspace, the destructive 'Import workspace — Replace all local data — destructive' row is only distinguished by an orange chevron and gray subtext, and looks like the neighboring rows. In the builder, 'Save routine' is the strongest control on a day with 0 exercises. The session summary dims the page behind it but the footer 'Finish workout' button shows through beneath the dialog.
findings.userConsequence: If the theme state is a real bug, the user can't tell which theme is active. The destructive row could be tapped by accident. A user can save an empty routine and see 'Save routine' before they have added anything.
findings.suggestedChange: Check that the selected theme chip matches the applied theme. Give the destructive action a clear warning color or a confirmation step. Disable 'Save routine' until a day has content, or explain what saving an empty day does. Make the summary dialog fully opaque.

strengths: The visual system is restrained and consistent across screens: the same blue accent, linen surfaces, bordered cards and monospace metadata are used throughout.
Dark and light themes have visibly parallel structure, and the dark workout and detail screens keep the same layout and hierarchy.

The workout screen is information-dense in a useful way: sections are separated with color rails (blue warm-up, main lift, purple accessory), entered sets are visible as chips, and 'saved 6/6 sets' with 'Finish workout' is anchored in a sticky bar.
The exercise history drawer is clear and compact: dates, volume, and previous sets per version are all scannable, and the current session is highlighted.
Local-first messaging on Workspace is explicit, with data counts, backup download, persistence warning and an explained undo point.
The three-step Today onboarding and the Import flow (paste, resolve names, confirm with weekly preview) form a clear linear path for the copy/paste AI workflow.
The import error state offers a concrete recovery action ('Copy recovery prompt for your AI chat').
The navigation drawer is simple: icons with text labels, a clear active state, and no more than eight items.
limitations: Review was based only on the 27 frozen static screenshots; no live interaction, keyboard, screen-reader, focus, hover or animation behavior was checked.
Contrast was judged by eye only. I did not measure ratios, so contrast claims are impressions rather than pass/fail results.
Only three desktop captures and four dark captures exist, so desktop and dark parity for the other screens is not evidenced. Responsive behavior outside 390x844 and 1280x900 was not checked.
The dark Workspace capture shows 'linen' selected while appearing dark; I could not determine from the image whether this is a real bug or a capture artifact.
Long pages (Prompts, Profile, Library, Import confirm) were captured only above the fold, so content below was not reviewed.
I did not validate any finding against source code or the running app, and I did not read other reviewers' output or compare with earlier rounds (this is the baseline).
